claims.statement: In adults with alcohol dependence treated as outpatients in double-blind trials, mostly after detoxification and with counselling or another psychosocial treatment in both groups, naltrexone tablets at the dose used in most trials compared with placebo reduced return to heavy drinking (in most trials 5 or more drinks in a day for men, 4 or more for women) during 12 to 52 weeks of treatment: across 19 trials pooled in a review for the US Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, 728 of 1,593 people on naltrexone (46 in 100) and 698 of 1,282 on placebo (54 in 100) returned to heavy drinking (crude totals, editors' arithmetic), a pooled difference of 9 in 100 (risk difference −0.09, 95% CI −0.13 to −0.04; 12 people treated for one to benefit) (Jonas et al., 2014; funded by the agency; no conflicts declared). Its 2023 update found a risk ratio of 0.81 (0.72 to 0.90; 23 trials, 3,170 people), and a Cochrane review of naltrexone in any form, mostly the same tablets, 0.83 (0.76 to 0.90; 28 trials, 4,433 people) (McPheeters et al., 2023; Rösner et al., 2010). The effect on staying off alcohol completely was small or unclear: risk difference −0.05 (−0.10 to −0.002) in 2014, risk ratio 0.93 (0.87 to 0.99) in 2023 and 0.96 (0.92 to 1.00) in the Cochrane review. People on naltrexone drank on about 5 fewer days in every 100 (−5.1 percentage points, −7.16 to −3.04) and drank heavily on about 4 fewer (−4.3, −7.60 to −0.91). Nausea (risk ratio 1.73, 1.51 to 1.98), dizziness (1.99, 1.47 to 2.69) and vomiting (1.53, 1.23 to 1.91) were more common, about 1 more person in 48 stopped a trial because of side effects (number needed to harm 48, 30 to 112), and serious adverse events were not more frequent (risk difference −0.02, −0.05 to 0.00; 9 trials). A higher oral dose and a long-acting injection were each tested in only 2 or 3 trials, without a clear effect on return to heavy drinking. Head to head, naltrexone and acamprosate did not differ (return to heavy drinking risk ratio 1.02, 0.93 to 1.11; 4 trials, more than half of the people in one US trial). Evidence on deaths, injuries and quality of life is insufficient. The three reviews share most of their trials and are one body of evidence, not three. Most participants were White men in their 40s with moderate to severe dependence who had stopped drinking before starting, and effects in people still drinking, with mild disorder or without counselling are uncertain. Certainty: moderate. Status: replicated.
claims.magnitude: Jonas et al. 2014 (oral naltrexone, main dose group, against placebo): return to heavy drinking RD −0.09 (95% CI −0.13 to −0.04), 19 trials, 2875 participants, I² 43.7%, NNT 12 (8 to 26), moderate strength of evidence; crude totals 728/1593 (45.7%) against 698/1282 (54.4%) (editors' arithmetic from Figure 3); return to any drinking RD −0.05 (−0.10 to −0.002), 16 trials, 2347, NNT 20 (11 to 500); percentage of drinking days WMD −5.4 (−7.5 to −3.2); heavy drinking days −4.1 (−7.6 to −0.61); withdrawal from trials because of adverse events NNH 48 (30 to 112), 17 trials, 2743. McPheeters et al. 2023: return to heavy drinking RR 0.81 (0.72 to 0.90), 23 trials, 3170, moderate; return to any drinking 0.93 (0.87 to 0.99), 16 trials, 2347, moderate; percentage of drinking days −5.1 (−7.16 to −3.04), 15 trials; heavy drinking days −4.3 (−7.60 to −0.91), 7 trials; any dose, return to heavy drinking 0.86 (0.80 to 0.93), 27 trials, 4645; higher oral dose 0.93 (0.84 to 1.01), 2 trials, and injection 1.00 (0.82 to 1.21), 2 trials, both low; nausea RR 1.73 (1.51 to 1.98), dizziness 1.99 (1.47 to 2.69), vomiting 1.53 (1.23 to 1.91); acamprosate against naltrexone, return to any drinking 1.03 (0.96 to 1.10), 3 trials, 800, return to heavy drinking 1.02 (0.93 to 1.11), 4 trials, 1141; deaths 1 against 2 (6 trials, 1738), insufficient. Rösner et al. 2010 (Cochrane): return to heavy drinking RR 0.83 (0.76 to 0.90), 28 trials, 4433, NNTB 9.09 (6.66 to 14.28); return to any drinking 0.96 (0.92 to 1.00), 27 trials, 4693 (fixed effect 0.95, 0.92 to 0.98); drinking days MD −3.89 (−5.75 to −2.04); nausea RD 0.10 (0.07 to 0.13); serious adverse events RD −0.02 (−0.05 to 0.00), 9 trials; drop-out because of adverse events RR 1.60 (1.15 to 2.23), 22 trials.
